FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Part 68) (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Methods for Sampling and Test for Petroleum and Related Products of Natural or Synthetic Origin 
(excluding bitumen) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products 
Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1967 based on IP 183/63T and subsequently, amendment no. 1, November 
1993 was issued. The first revision has been brought out to keep pace with the latest technological developments 
and international practices. In this revision no major changes have been made. 


The composition of the Committee, responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 
In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or 


calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 “Rules for rounding off numerical 
values (second revision)’. 


IS 1448 (Part 68) : 2023 


Indian Standard 
PETROLEUM AND ITS PRODUCTS — METHODS OF TEST 
PART 68 DETERMINATION OF EVAPORATION LOSS OF 


LUBRICATING GREASES (22 HOUR DRYING) 
(First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the method of test to 
determine the loss in mass by evaporation of 
lubricating greases under prescribed test conditions. 


2 OUTLINE OF THE METHOD 


The evaporation cell is filled with grease, weighed 
and placed in a bath maintained at the desired test 
temperature which is normally in the range of 99 *C 
to 150 °C. Heated air is passed over its surface for 
22 hours. After the test, evaporation cell is 
reweighed and evaporation loss is calculated from 
the loss in weight of the sample. 


3 SIGNIFICANCE AND USE 


This test is used to indicate the degree of volatile 
matter present in a grease and is used mainly for 
specification purpose. No correlation with field 
services has been established. 


4 APPARATUS 


4.1 The assembly of apparatus, as shown in Fig. 1, 
consists of the following major parts. 


4.1.1 Evaporation Cell 


Constructed from stainless steel with air heating coil 
of tinned copper tubing, conforming to the form and 
dimensions shown in Fig. 1. 


4.1.2 Sample Cup 


As shown in Fig. 2. It is recommended that the 
weight shall not exceed 200 g. The cup, hood, outlet 
tube and orifice shall be constructed of 18 percent 
chromium and 8 percent nickel alloy steel. The 
sample cup shall be screwed to the hood and the 
latter screwed to the outlet tube of the cover. The 
cover and cell shall make an air-tight joint. 


4.1.3 Air Supply System 


Capable of supplying to the cell the required flow 
of dry air free of entrained particles. A 400 mm 
length pipe with a 25 mm diameter packed with 
glass wool has been found satisfactory for filtering 
the air. 


4.1.4 Oil Bath 


Oil bath of sufficient depth to allow immersion of 
the evaporation cell to the proper level indicated in 
Fig. 1 and capable of being controlled to within + 
0.5 °C of the desired temperature and with a 
maximum variation, throughout the bath, of 0.5 *C. 
Circulation of the oil-heating medium by a pump or 
stirrer is recommended. Sufficient heat capacity 
shall be provided to return the bath to the required 
temperature within 30 minutes after immersion of 
the cell. 


NOTE — Other constant-temperature baths may be used if 
they are equivalent in heat capacity and thermal gradient 
characteristics to the oil bath.

Thermometers conforming to the following requirements shall be used:

4.1.6 Flow Meter 


A calibrated flow meter to deliver air at the rate of 
2.58 litres/min + 0:02 litre/min between 16 °C and 
29 °C (2 litres/min at standard temperature and 
pressure). It shall be furnished with an air 
adjustment needle valve as shown in Fig. 1. 


4.1.7 Balance — Capable of weighing to the nearest 
mg 


4.1.8 Spatula 
5 SAMPLING 


Approximately 20 g sample is required to fill the 
sample cup for a single run. Examine the sample for 
any indication of non-homogeneity such as oil 
separation, phase changes, or overall contamination. 
If any abnormal conditions are found, obtain a new 
sample for test. 


6 PROCEDURE 


6.1 The test shall be carried out in duplicate. 


6.2 Clean all components of sample cup and hood 
assembly. Verify unrestricted air flow through 
tubing on test cell. Check that the oil bath is filled 
with a sufficient quantity of fluid to allow 
submersion of the evaporation cell to the proper 
level. Check flow meter. 


6.3 Weigh the clean sample cup and hood to the 
nearest milligram. 


6.4 Remove the hood and fill the cup, avoiding any 
occlusion of air. Smooth the surface level with the 
rim of the cup using a straight-edged spatula. 
Remove with a clean cloth any grease, which may 
remain on the rim or threads of the cup. 


6.5 Screw the hood tightly on the cup without 
disturbing the smoothed grease surface. 


6.6 Weigh the assembly and calculate the net weight 
of the sample. 


6.7 Bring the oil bath to desired test temperature. 


6.8 With the cover in place, but without the hood and 


sample cup attached, immerse the cell in the oil bath 
as shown in Fig. 1 for at least 30 min. with clean dry 
air flowing through the cell at rate of 2 litres/min. 


6.9 Remove the cover, screw the weighed hood sand 
sample cup into place and replace the cover. Tighten 
the three knurled cover screws to prevent air leakage 
under the cover. 


6.10 Pass clean dry air through the cell at the 
prescribed rate for 22 h + 5 min. 


6.11 After 22 h, remove the assembled sample cup 
and hood from the cell and allow to cool to room 
temperature. Determine the mass of the sample to 
the nearest milligram. 


7 CALCULATION 


Calculate the evaporation loss of the sample as 
follows: 


S-W 
5 


х 100 


Evaporation loss, percent by weight = 


where 


S = initial mass, in g, of the sample; and 
W = mass, in g, of the sample after test. 


IS 1448 (Part 68) : 2023 


8 REPORTING 


Report the geometric mean of the two 
determinations as percentage evaporation loss at the 
test temperature. 


9 PRECISION 
9.1 General 


The following criteria shall be used for judging the 
acceptability of results except for those results 
having an evaporation loss of less than 2 percent. 


9.2 Repeatability 


The difference between two test results, obtained by 
the same operator with the same apparatus under 
constant operating conditions on identical test 
material in the normal and correct operation of the 
test method, exceed 10 percent of the smaller 
amount in only one case in twenty. 


9.3 Reproducibility 


The difference between two single and independent 
results obtained by different operators working in 
different laboratories on identical test material 
would in the normal and correct operation of the test 
method, exceed 22 percent of the smaller amount in 
only one case in twenty. 


IS 1448 (Part 68) : 2023
